canada.intro:
Canada is a huge country of mountains, lakes, coastlines and cosmopolitan cities. Its food scene reflects immigrants from around the world, along with strong regional traditions and fresh local ingredients.

This page explains what Canada is known for, what to eat and where to go, and helps you use the listings to compare ratings, photos and locations before you choose a table.

sections.body:
Canada is known for the Rocky Mountains, Niagara Falls, the Northern Lights, ice hockey and its friendly people. Its cities, from Vancouver to Halifax, each have their own character, and the country has two official languages, English and French.

Seasons shape life and food, from summer patios to cozy winter comfort dishes.

Poutine, fries topped with cheese curds and gravy, is the iconic dish from Quebec. Maple syrup, butter tarts, Nanaimo bars and tourtiere, a spiced meat pie, are classic sweets and savories. Smoked meat sandwiches in Montreal, Atlantic lobster rolls, salmon on the west coast and Alberta beef are regional highlights.

Canadian cities are known for excellent Chinese, Indian, Korean, Italian and Middle Eastern food, and a growing craft beer and wine scene.

Vancouver and Victoria offer ocean and mountain scenery, while Banff, Jasper and Whistler are mountain destinations. Toronto and Montreal are big cities with great food, Quebec City has European charm, and Niagara Falls is a classic stop.

The Atlantic provinces offer coastal villages, and Newfoundland has dramatic cliffs and icebergs.

sections.h2: How to choose a restaurant in Canada
sections.body:

Book ahead for weekend dinners in big cities and in mountain towns during peak season.

Tipping is expected, usually 15 to 20 percent of the pre tax bill. Prices on menus usually exclude tax, which is added at the end. Restaurants in smaller towns may close early in the evening.

canada/alberta.intro:
Alberta is a western province with the Canadian Rockies, wide prairies and a strong ranching tradition.

This page explains what Alberta is known for, what to eat and where to go, and helps you use the listings to compare ratings, photos and locations before you choose a table.

sections.body:
The province is known for Banff and Jasper national parks, glaciers and turquoise lakes such as Lake Louise and Moraine Lake. Calgary hosts the Stampede, a famous rodeo festival, and Edmonton is the capital with a lively festival scene.

Outdoor activities, from skiing to hiking, shape life here.

Alberta is known for its beef, with steakhouses serving local cuts, and for Calgary's claim as the home of the Caesar cocktail. Look for bison dishes, pierogies, farm to table menus and craft beer. Breakfast spots serve hearty plates, and bakeries sell cinnamon rolls and local treats.

Mountain lodges offer fine dining with views.

Banff has hot springs, gondolas and lakes, Jasper offers wildlife and dark skies, and the Icefields Parkway is one of the world's most scenic drives. Calgary has the Stampede and a lively food scene, and Drumheller has dinosaur museums.

In winter, ski resorts such as Lake Louise draw visitors.

canada/alberta/banff.intro:
Banff is a mountain town inside Canada's oldest national park, surrounded by snowy peaks and glacial lakes.

This page explains what Banff is known for, what to eat and where to go, and helps you use the listings to compare ratings, photos and locations before you choose a table.

sections.body:
The town is known for Banff Avenue and its views of Cascade Mountain, the Banff Gondola, the hot springs and nearby Lake Louise and Moraine Lake. Wildlife such as elk is often seen in town.

It is a World Heritage site and a base for hiking, skiing and sightseeing.

Dining ranges from lodge restaurants with mountain views to casual pubs and cafes. Look for Alberta beef, bison, elk, trout and hearty comfort dishes. Bakeries and cafes serve pastries and coffee, and local craft beer and spirits are on offer.

After a hike, poutine and burgers are popular.

The Banff Gondola, the Upper Hot Springs, Lake Minnewanka, Lake Louise and Moraine Lake are highlights. The Bow Falls and Johnston Canyon are easy walks, and the Icefields Parkway leads north to Jasper.

In winter, Sunshine Village and Mount Norquay offer skiing.

Check the address on the map and use the phone number to confirm opening hours before you go. Banff Avenue has many choices but fills up quickly, so book dinner ahead in summer and winter. For quieter meals, look in side streets.

Summer is the busiest, and winter is cold but beautiful. Parking is limited, so use the shuttle for lakes. Park passes are required.

canada/alberta/calgary.intro:
Calgary is a modern city on the edge of the Rockies, known for its western heritage and for being a gateway to Banff.

This page explains what Calgary is known for, what to eat and where to go, and helps you use the listings to compare ratings, photos and locations before you choose a table.

sections.body:
The city is known for the Calgary Stampede, held every July, the Calgary Tower and its bright sunny days. Its downtown has a pedestrian bridge network, and the nearby mountains are an hour away.

Calgary has a thriving restaurant scene, with many neighborhoods having their own cafes and bars.

Alberta beef is the star, from steakhouse cuts to burgers. The Caesar cocktail, made with clam tomato juice, was invented here. Look for bison, local craft beer, Vietnamese and Chinese food, and Calgary style ginger beef.

Pancake breakfasts are a Stampede tradition.

The Calgary Tower, the Glenbow area, Heritage Park and Prince's Island Park are highlights. The Calgary Zoo and Telus Spark science center are good for families, and Banff is a short drive away.

The Stampede grounds are lively in July.

Check the address on the map and use the phone number to confirm opening hours before you go. Neighborhoods such as Inglewood, Kensington and 17th Avenue are popular for dining. Book ahead during the Stampede.

Winters are cold and summers are sunny. The Stampede is very busy. Tipping 15 to 20 percent is expected.

canada/alberta/jasper.intro:
Jasper is a mountain town in the largest national park in the Canadian Rockies, quieter and wilder than Banff.

This page explains what Jasper is known for, what to eat and where to go, and helps you use the listings to compare ratings, photos and locations before you choose a table.

sections.body:
The town is known for its wildlife, including elk, bears and mountain goats, for Maligne Lake and Spirit Island, and for its dark sky preserve, where the stars are bright. The Jasper SkyTram climbs to alpine views.

The town has a small, friendly feel.

Restaurants serve hearty mountain food, with Alberta beef, bison, trout and hearty soups. Cafes and bakeries are popular after hikes, and pubs serve craft beer and burgers. Look for local ingredients and seasonal menus.

Because the town is small, many places close early. Portions are often generous, and many restaurants offer vegetarian, vegan and gluten free choices, so it is easy to find something for every table.

Maligne Canyon, Maligne Lake, the SkyTram, Pyramid Lake and Athabasca Falls are highlights. The Icefields Parkway links Jasper to Banff, and the Columbia Icefield is a major stop.

Stargazing and wildlife viewing are popular.

British Columbia is Canada's Pacific province, with coastal rainforest, snowy mountains, islands and the Okanagan wine region.

This page explains what British Columbia is known for, what to eat and where to go, and helps you use the listings to compare ratings, photos and locations before you choose a table.

sections.h2: What British Columbia is known for
sections.body:
The province is known for Vancouver, Victoria, Whistler and the Okanagan Valley. It has a mild coast, big mountains and a strong culture of outdoor activity and local food. Indigenous cultures are part of the region's identity.

Its food culture favors fresh, local, and sustainable ingredients.

Fresh seafood is the highlight, with salmon, Dungeness crab, spot prawns and oysters. Sushi and Asian food are excellent, thanks to large communities from Japan, China and elsewhere. Nanaimo bars, a layered chocolate dessert, are a local classic.

The Okanagan makes fruit, wine and craft beer, and farm markets are popular.

sections.h2: Places to visit in British Columbia
sections.body:
Vancouver has Stanley Park and Granville Island, Victoria has gardens and the harbor, and Whistler has skiing and hiking. Tofino has surf beaches and rainforest, and the Okanagan offers lakes and wineries.

Whale watching tours run from several coastal towns.

canada/british-columbia/vancouver.intro:
Vancouver is a coastal city between mountains and ocean, known for its parks, diverse food and outdoor lifestyle.

This page explains what Vancouver is known for, what to eat and where to go, and helps you use the listings to compare ratings, photos and locations before you choose a table.

sections.body:
The city is known for Stanley Park, Granville Island Public Market, Gastown's steam clock and views of the North Shore mountains. It is a gateway to Whistler and Vancouver Island.

Its neighborhoods, such as Chinatown, Main Street and Kitsilano, each have a different food identity.

Seafood is the specialty, with wild salmon, Dungeness crab, oysters and spot prawns. Vancouver is considered one of the best places in North America for sushi and also for dim sum and Chinese food in nearby Richmond. Ramen, Korean fried chicken and Indian food are popular.

Craft beer, coffee and farm to table menus are also strong.

Stanley Park and its seawall, Granville Island, Capilano Suspension Bridge and Grouse Mountain are highlights. Gastown and Chinatown are lively, and the beaches at Kitsilano and English Bay are popular in summer.

Whistler and Victoria are day or overnight trips.

Check the address on the map and use the phone number to confirm opening hours before you go. Choose by neighborhood, such as Gastown for modern cooking, Richmond for Chinese food and Main Street for cafes. Book for weekend dinners.

Rain is common in autumn and winter, so bring a jacket. Tipping 15 to 20 percent is standard. Many restaurants offer vegetarian and vegan options.

canada/british-columbia/victoria.intro:
Victoria is the capital of British Columbia, on the southern tip of Vancouver Island, with an English garden feel and a pretty harbor.

This page explains what Victoria is known for, what to eat and where to go, and helps you use the listings to compare ratings, photos and locations before you choose a table.

sections.body:
The city is known for the Inner Harbour, the Parliament Buildings, Butchart Gardens and its afternoon tea tradition. It has a mild climate, flower baskets on lamp posts and a relaxed pace.

Whale watching and kayaking leave from the harbor.

Afternoon tea is a classic experience, with sandwiches, scones and pastries. Seafood is excellent, including fish and chips, fresh crab and oysters. The city has a strong craft beer and coffee culture, and farm to table menus use island produce.

Chinatown and Fisherman's Wharf add variety.

The Inner Harbour, the Royal BC Museum, Butchart Gardens, Craigdarroch Castle and Fisherman's Wharf are the highlights. Beacon Hill Park is a large green space, and the Galloping Goose trail is good for cycling.

The BC Ferries ride from Vancouver is scenic.

The harbor area has many options, and neighborhoods such as Fernwood and Oak Bay offer local cafes.

Summer is the busiest, and winters are mild but rainy. Book whale watching in advance.

canada/british-columbia/whistler.intro:
Whistler is a mountain resort village north of Vancouver, known for large ski areas and outdoor activities all year.

This page explains what Whistler is known for, what to eat and where to go, and helps you use the listings to compare ratings, photos and locations before you choose a table.

sections.body:
The village is known for Whistler Blackcomb ski resort, the Peak 2 Peak gondola and a pedestrian village with shops and restaurants. It hosted the Winter Olympics in 2010.

In summer, mountain biking, hiking and lakes draw visitors.

Dining ranges from casual pubs and poutine to fine dining with mountain views. Look for seafood, local game, craft beer and bakery treats. After skiing, apres ski bars offer drinks and snacks, and cafes serve hot chocolate and pastries.

Many restaurants use local and seasonal ingredients. Portions are often generous, and many restaurants offer vegetarian, vegan and gluten free choices, so it is easy to find something for every table.

The Peak 2 Peak gondola, the Whistler Village stroll, Lost Lake and the Squamish Sea to Sky Gondola are highlights. The Sea to Sky Highway from Vancouver is a scenic drive.

Summer brings biking and hiking.

canada/manitoba.intro:
Manitoba is a prairie province in central Canada, with wide skies, lakes and a lively capital, Winnipeg.

This page explains what Manitoba is known for, what to eat and where to go, and helps you use the listings to compare ratings, photos and locations before you choose a table.

sections.body:
The province is known for Churchill, where polar bears are seen in autumn, for beluga whales and for the Northern Lights. Winnipeg is a cultural center, with the Forks market and an arts scene.

The province has a strong Indigenous, Icelandic, Ukrainian and Mennonite heritage.

Look for pickerel, a local freshwater fish, bison, perogies, cabbage rolls and Icelandic pastries such as vinarterta. Winnipeg is known for its Jewish deli, its Ukrainian food and its Mennonite sausage. Saskatoon berry pie is a classic prairie dessert.

Craft beer and coffee are growing in popularity. Portions are often generous, and many restaurants offer vegetarian, vegan and gluten free choices, so it is easy to find something for every table.

Winnipeg has the Canadian Museum for Human Rights, the Forks and the Assiniboine Park Zoo. Churchill offers polar bear and beluga tours, and Riding Mountain National Park has wildlife and lakes.

Gimli is a lakeside Icelandic town.

canada/manitoba/winnipeg.intro:
Winnipeg is a prairie city at the meeting of two rivers, with a strong cultural scene and some of the most distinctive food in central Canada.

This page explains what Winnipeg is known for, what to eat and where to go, and helps you use the listings to compare ratings, photos and locations before you choose a table.

sections.body:
The city is known for the Forks, a meeting place with markets and shops, the Canadian Museum for Human Rights and the Exchange District of historic buildings. It has a very active arts scene and an annual folk festival.

Winters are long and cold, and the city has skating trails on frozen rivers.

Look for pickerel, perogies, cabbage rolls and Ukrainian dishes, Jewish deli sandwiches and Icelandic treats. The Forks Market offers local food stalls, and the city has strong Filipino, Indian and Ethiopian options. Local craft beer and bakeries are popular.

Saskatoon berry pie is a regional dessert.

The Forks, the Canadian Museum for Human Rights, the Exchange District, the Manitoba Museum and the Assiniboine Park Zoo are the highlights. The Winnipeg Art Gallery houses Inuit art.

In winter, skating on the river trail is a local tradition.

canada/newfoundland-and-labrador.intro:
Newfoundland and Labrador is Canada's most easterly province, with rugged cliffs, fishing villages and a warm, welcoming culture.

This page explains what Newfoundland and Labrador is known for, what to eat and where to go, and helps you use the listings to compare ratings, photos and locations before you choose a table.

sections.h2: What Newfoundland and Labrador is known for
sections.body:
The province is known for icebergs and whales along its coast, for Gros Morne National Park and for L'Anse aux Meadows, where Vikings once settled. St. John's, the capital, is known for its colorful houses and lively pubs.

Local humor, music and hospitality are famous.

Seafood is central, with cod, crab, mussels and scallops. Traditional dishes include fish and brewis, cod tongues, toutons, fried bread dough with molasses, and Jiggs dinner, a boiled meal of salt beef and vegetables. Partridgeberry and bakeapple, a local berry, are used in jams and desserts.

Local beers and screech rum are part of the culture.

sections.h2: Places to visit in Newfoundland and Labrador
sections.body:
St. John's has Signal Hill, colorful Jellybean Row and George Street pubs. Cape Spear is the most easterly point in North America, and Gros Morne has fjords and hiking. Twillingate and Bonavista offer icebergs, whales and puffins.

L'Anse aux Meadows is a World Heritage site.

sections.h2: What St. John's is known for
sections.body:
The city is known for Signal Hill, Jellybean Row, George Street's many pubs and the nearby Cape Spear lookout. Whales and icebergs can sometimes be seen close to the shore.

The warm local culture, with folk music and storytelling, adds to the charm.

Fresh cod, crab, mussels and scallops are common, along with fish and chips and fish cakes. Try toutons, Jiggs dinner, and cod tongues. Local berries, such as partridgeberry and bakeapple, appear in desserts and jams.

Pubs serve local beer and live music in the evening. Portions are often generous, and many restaurants offer vegetarian, vegan and gluten free choices, so it is easy to find something for every table.

sections.h2: Places to visit in St. John's
sections.body:
Signal Hill, Cape Spear, Quidi Vidi village and the Rooms museum are the highlights. A boat tour shows puffins and whales, and the East Coast Trail offers coastal hikes.

George Street is the heart of nightlife.

sections.h2: What Nova Scotia is known for
sections.body:
The province is known for the Cabot Trail, one of the most scenic drives in Canada, for Peggy's Cove lighthouse and for the world's highest tides in the Bay of Fundy. Halifax, the capital, is a lively harbor city.

Music and seafaring heritage are central to its identity.

Seafood is the star, with lobster, scallops, mussels and haddock. Lobster rolls, chowder and Digby scallops are classics, and Donair, a local meat sandwich, is popular in Halifax. Oatcakes, blueberries and maple products are common.

Wines from the Annapolis Valley and craft beer are growing. Portions are often generous, and many restaurants offer vegetarian, vegan and gluten free choices, so it is easy to find something for every table.

sections.h2: Places to visit in Nova Scotia
sections.body:
The Cabot Trail, Peggy's Cove, Lunenburg and Fundy tidal bore rafting are highlights. The Annapolis Valley has vineyards, and Cape Breton Island has hiking and music.

Halifax has a harbor waterfront and a citadel.

The city is known for the Halifax Citadel, the Waterfront Boardwalk, the Public Gardens and a busy harbor. Its pubs have live music most nights, and the city is the gateway to Peggy's Cove and the Annapolis Valley.

History, from the Titanic to the Halifax Explosion, is part of local memory.

Seafood is the highlight, with lobster rolls, chowder, scallops and fish and chips. The donair, a local sandwich with sweet sauce, is the city's late night favorite. Craft beer, local oysters and blueberry desserts are widely available.

Farmers markets sell local produce and baked goods. Portions are often generous, and many restaurants offer vegetarian, vegan and gluten free choices, so it is easy to find something for every table.

The Citadel, the Waterfront Boardwalk, the Maritime Museum of the Atlantic and Point Pleasant Park are popular. Peggy's Cove and Lunenburg are day trips, and the Annapolis Valley offers wineries.

Pier 21 shows immigration history.

The province is known for Toronto's skyline, Niagara Falls, the capital Ottawa and thousands of lakes. Niagara has vineyards that make ice wine, and Prince Edward County is known for farms and wine.

Immigration has made Ontario's food scene among the most diverse in the world.

Toronto offers dishes from nearly every culture, from Chinese and Indian to Caribbean and Italian. Peameal bacon sandwiches, butter tarts and fried dough pastries are local favorites. Ottawa is known for its fried dough pastries and a growing food scene.

Ice wine and craft beer are regional specialties.

Toronto has the CN Tower, the Distillery District and the St. Lawrence Market. Niagara Falls offers boat rides and wineries, Ottawa has Parliament Hill and the Rideau Canal, and the Muskoka lakes are popular for summer.

Kingston and the Thousand Islands add history.

The tourist area has many restaurants, attractions and hotels.

Restaurants range from casual burgers and pizza to fine dining with falls views. Try local ice wine and Niagara peaches in season. Niagara on the Lake offers farm to table meals, wineries and bakeries.

Butter tarts and fudge are popular sweets. Portions are often generous, and many restaurants offer vegetarian, vegan and gluten free choices, so it is easy to find something for every table.

The boat ride to the base of the falls, the Journey Behind the Falls, the Skylon Tower and Clifton Hill are highlights. Niagara on the Lake and the wine route are a short drive.

The Tulip Festival in May is a highlight.

The ByWard Market is a hub for dining, with cafes, bistros and food stalls. fried dough pastries are a classic treat, and poutine is common. The city has good Lebanese, Indian and Asian food, craft beer and farm to table menus.

Maple products and local cheese are sold in the market. Portions are often generous, and many restaurants offer vegetarian, vegan and gluten free choices, so it is easy to find something for every table.

The city is also known for sports, festivals and a growing tech scene.

Toronto is one of the world's most diverse food cities. Try Chinese dim sum, Indian curry, Caribbean jerk, Portuguese grills, Korean barbecue and Italian pasta. Peameal bacon sandwiches at the market, butter tarts and poutine are local flavors.

Craft breweries, bakeries and coffee shops are everywhere. Portions are often generous, and many restaurants offer vegetarian, vegan and gluten free choices, so it is easy to find something for every table.

sections.h2: What Prince Edward Island is known for
sections.body:

Food is an important part of island life, with strong farm and sea traditions.

Lobster suppers in church halls are a classic, along with fresh mussels, oysters and scallops. PEI potatoes are famous, and the island also grows strawberries and blueberries. Look for chowder, fish and chips and ice cream.

Local craft beer and wine are growing. Portions are often generous, and many restaurants offer vegetarian, vegan and gluten free choices, so it is easy to find something for every table.

sections.h2: Places to visit in Prince Edward Island

Cavendish and the Green Gables house, Prince Edward Island National Park, Charlottetown's waterfront and the lighthouses are highlights. The Confederation Trail is a long cycling route.

Oyster tours and farm visits are popular.

The harbor is the center of city life.

Seafood is the headline, with lobster, mussels, oysters and chowder. Many restaurants use island produce and potatoes, and cafes serve local ice cream and baked goods. Craft beer and wine from the island are popular.

A food tour of the city is a good introduction. Portions are often generous, and many restaurants offer vegetarian, vegan and gluten free choices, so it is easy to find something for every table.

sections.body:
The province is known for Montreal's festivals, Quebec City's old town, the Laurentian mountains and a strong French identity. Its food culture mixes French technique with local ingredients such as maple and cheese curds.

Winter carnival and cozy cabins are part of the experience.

Poutine, tourtiere, pea soup, maple syrup treats and smoked meat sandwiches are classics. Sugar shacks in spring serve big maple meals, and Quebec cheeses are excellent. Bagels from Montreal are famous, and crepes and pastries add French touches.

Local cider, including ice cider, is a specialty.

Montreal has Old Montreal, Mount Royal and the Jean Talon market. Quebec City has the walled old town and the Chateau Frontenac. The Laurentians offer skiing and lakes, and the Gaspe Peninsula offers dramatic coastline.

Maple season in March and April is special.

canada/quebec/montreal.intro:
Montreal is a bilingual city with European charm, an energetic arts scene and some of the most loved food in Canada.

This page explains what Montreal is known for, what to eat and where to go, and helps you use the listings to compare ratings, photos and locations before you choose a table.

sections.body:
The city is known for Old Montreal's cobbled streets, Mount Royal, the Notre Dame Basilica and an endless calendar of festivals. Its neighborhoods, such as the Plateau and Mile End, are filled with cafes and bakeries.

Montreal is known for its nightlife and for its jazz and comedy festivals.

Montreal style bagels, baked in wood fired ovens, and smoked meat sandwiches are iconic. Poutine, tourtiere and Quebec cheeses are common. The city has excellent French bistros, bakeries and brunch spots, and the Jean Talon market offers fresh produce.

Maple treats and ice cider are good gifts.

Old Montreal, the Notre Dame Basilica, Mount Royal, the Jean Talon market and the Underground City are highlights. The Plateau and Mile End are fun for walks.

Quebec City is a few hours away.

canada/quebec/quebec-city.intro:
Quebec City is the only walled city north of Mexico, with a European feel, a grand castle hotel and a strong French identity.

This page explains what Quebec City is known for, what to eat and where to go, and helps you use the listings to compare ratings, photos and locations before you choose a table.

sections.h2: What Quebec City is known for
sections.body:
The city is known for the Chateau Frontenac, the cobbled streets of Old Quebec, the Plains of Abraham and the Winter Carnival. Its lower town is full of shops, cafes and restaurants.

It is a place for strolls, history and cozy dinners.

Look for tourtiere, pea soup, poutine, maple desserts and Quebec cheese. French bistros serve duck, rabbit and local game, and bakeries sell fresh pastries. Cider and ice cider are specialties.

In winter, hot chocolate and maple taffy on snow are fun treats. Portions are often generous, and many restaurants offer vegetarian, vegan and gluten free choices, so it is easy to find something for every table.

sections.h2: Places to visit in Quebec City
sections.body:
The Chateau Frontenac, the Petit Champlain district, the Citadelle and the Plains of Abraham are highlights. Montmorency Falls and the Ile d'Orleans are short trips.

The Winter Carnival in February is a big event.
